brief: Fed Governor Waller said he expects two additional rate hikes to be appropriate, which would raise the funds rate to 4.25-4.50%, if data keep coming in as expected; the hikes need not be at consecutive meetings but should occur within an acceptable period of time. He noted eight SEP participants see rates 50bp higher by end-2027 and gave an example of three 25bp hikes total. Waller said his shift followed a preponderance of evidence that labor-market strength and persistent inflation forces have changed the policy risk balance, naming three forces that have undermined his faith in the 2% path: the unresolved Middle East conflict, the AI buildout raising tech consumer prices, and new-tariff risk. He also endorsed the Fed's current SEP/dot-plot communication approach, implying he would oppose scrapping it. Goldman Sachs continues to expect one 25bp December hike (to 4-4.25%) and has lowered its probability that the FOMC skips December, because Waller's speech is a hawkish shift versus his earlier emphasis on three-month annualized core PCE, now 2.0%; GS still expects inflation data to improve enough by March to convince most of the FOMC further hikes are unnecessary.
